page: Microsoft Azure E4d_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance is powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor on x86_64 architecture. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs split across 2 physical cores utilizing hyper-threading (2 threads per core). Cache allocation includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 (f and vnni variants), AES, and SHA-NI cryptographic hardware support. The server includes 32.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB RAM-to-core ratio, alongside 161 GB of integrated local SSD storage. It features no GPUs and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results highlight balanced single-threaded execution alongside constrained multi-threaded scaling due to the 4 vCPU topology. In synthetic compute evaluations, single-core metrics fall within the middle 50% tier, showing a Geekbench single-core score of 1640.0, a stress-ng single-core score of 1895.98, and static web serving throughput of 6.55 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded throughput ranks in the lower brackets, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 3498.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 5903.46. Memory-intensive tests demonstrate steady uncached bandwidth at 28.99 GB/sec read and 25.08 GB/sec write, yielding an average PassMark memory score of 2331.58.

The primary efficiency tradeoff for the E4d_v5 lies in its heavy memory density combined with fast local NVMe/SSD caching relative to aggregate computing power. Because it limits raw processing scale to 2 physical cores, heavily parallel computational tasks such as 7B LLM inference (yielding 4.56 tokens/sec) and multi-threaded decompression are bottlenecks. However, for workloads requiring sizable in-memory working sets alongside local scratch space without the cost of high core allocations, the hardware layout provides an economical configuration.

Appropriate deployment scenarios include intermediate relational and key-value database caches, Redis instances, middle-tier enterprise application servers, and memory-heavy web hosting environments. The 161 GB local SSD also fits temporary logging, staging files, and scratch storage requirements.
description: Microsoft Azure E4d_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores of a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor, paired with 32.0 GB of RAM (8.0 GB per core) and 161 GB of local SSD storage. Designed without an integrated GPU, the instance leverages Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization and supports AVX-512 and cryptographic hardware acceleration. Benchmark data demonstrates solid single-threaded performance, with average scores across standard CPU tests, web serving throughput, and memory bandwidth, alongside weaker multi-core compute throughput consistent with its 4-thread envelope. The high memory-to-vCPU ratio combined with direct local storage makes the E4d_v5 effective for in-memory databases, Redis deployments, caching layers, and enterprise applications that demand substantial RAM capacity without excessive processor overhead.
